prompt: Turn a day number 1-7 into its name with a switch that has a real default, and report whether that day falls on the weekend. Out-of-range numbers must not slip through.
explanation: A switch on an int maps a small set of known values to results, and the default branch is what keeps the method total -- without it, day 8 would fall past every case and reach the end of the method. Returning straight out of each case means no break statements are needed and no case can fall through into the next. isWeekend needs no switch at all: a single boolean expression is clearer than two cases plus a default.
hints: Each case can return its name directly, so you never need a break.
The default branch catches 0, 8, -3 and everything else in one place.
isWeekend is one line -- combine two == comparisons with ||.
